intelligence.enrichment: Water can disappear from view by seeping into a porous surface, by evaporating into water vapour, or by both processes depending on the surface. The surface and conditions determine whether liquid water enters the surface, changes into vapour, or does both. The learner correctly applies this rule: Water can disappear from view by seeping into a porous surface, by evaporating into water vapour, or by both processes depending on the surface. When water is no longer visible, it must have gone down into the surface underneath it.
